Priya / Monica —

Initial forensic summary below (high-level, I’ll attach raw artifacts):

Scope:
- Window examined: 2026-02-09T02:00:00Z through 2026-02-09T06:30:00Z (our maintenance window).
- Systems: inference-serving fleet (v3 runtime), edge LB, storage buckets (S3-us-west-2), and egress NAT gateways.

What we did:
- Reconstructed per-instance access logs and concatenated into access-log-reconciliation.csv (attached).
- Performed SHA256 manifest of all served request payloads and service logs; manifest is hash_manifest.txt (attached).
- Cross-checked egress flow records against Cloud NAT and firewall logs; flagged flows were resolved to infra-control plane endpoints and our vendor download mirrors.
- Verified KV/cache eviction logs and no large object uploads were recorded during window.

Findings (short):
- Access-log reconciliation shows all requests have matching ingress and processing records; there are no records of bulk read/download operations against customer storage during the window.
- Hash manifest reconciliation indicates no unexplained file divergence; all generated payloads match our stored artifacts (SHA256 checksums verified).
- A small set of connections to third-party mirror.ipnet.example (13.52.11.93) correspond to scheduled container image pulls from our mirror list; those pulls contained only internal runtime binaries, not customer payloads.

Conclusion: No evidence of customer data exfiltration based on the above checks. We are packaging the artifacts (access-log-reconciliation.csv, hash_manifest.txt, forensic_summary.txt) for your audit.

If you want deeper packet-level captures for a particular client IP we can produce PCAPs but that will take extra time and require approval.

Diego Fernandez
Lead Forensics Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attached is our formal attestation and supporting artifacts from the window you flagged. Summary of actions and findings: 

Actions taken

- SHA256 manifest verification of served payloads and log files.
- Cross-check of S3 access, container registry pulls, and KV cache operations.

Findings (official attestation)

- Egress flows observed are attributable to scheduled container image pulls and vendor mirrors; payloads for those flows are internal binaries (verified by checksum).
- No anomalous outbound transfers to unknown external IPs beyond expected maintenance operations.

Attached files:
- final_attestation.pdf (formal attestation signed by Redwood security lead)
